scope: The existing official source checkpoint exports to a published four-graph image-to-generation ONNX bundle plus three tokenizer files in the existing models-paddleocr Release. ORT CPU, OpenVINO CPU, and TensorRT 10.11 CUDA have full EOS generation evidence on the official sample. TensorRT library-built plans now also pass the full-generation official-image regression; four additional ChartQA human test charts generated exact checked-in expected tables and matched eight associated QA labels. These four curated samples are qualitative evidence, not a dataset accuracy metric.

tensorRtCudaEndToEnd.engineBuilderNote: The earlier null-engine report came from a test harness using the non-epsilon graph/profile pair and an attention-mask optimum of 512 with a KV optimum of 512; the mask length must equal past KV length + 1. TensorRT logged an internal reshape volume mismatch of 512 versus 513. The corrected test selects the epsilon graph used by the release plan and sets mask optimum to 513; TensorRtOnnxEngineBuilder then serialized the 51-input graph successfully. See tensorRtBuilderRegression.

fourGraphBundle.fp16LanguageHeadFinding: On this RTX 3060 laptop, TensorRT FP16 prefill/decode plans returned an all-zero lm_head logits tensor despite nonzero KV outputs. FP32 text prefill and decode plans restored the expected token sequence; the vision and token-embedding plans remain FP16.
fourGraphBundle.taskQualityBoundary: ORT CPU, OpenVINO CPU, and TensorRT CUDA each reached EOS and returned the same complete six-row table on one official sample. Four additional ChartQA human samples reproduced their expected tables and matched eight reference answers; this small curated set does not establish dataset-level accuracy or generalize to every chart style.

changes: The generic TensorRT host path now grows dynamic input buffers geometrically and reuses per-session output allocations instead of reallocating them on every token.
PaddleChart2TableTensorRtDeviceSession keeps the 48 KV tensors on CUDA in ping-pong banks; per decode step only logits, token embedding, and small attention/position inputs cross the host boundary.
TensorRtSession.RunDevice now sets all dynamic shapes before refreshing bindings and avoids duplicate BindAll/readiness work before enqueue.
The device path accepts optional TensorRT TF32 tactics for FP32 language plans; the verified output remains identical on the official sample.
kvBufferOptimization.contractTest: PaddleChart2TableOnnxSessionTests.FourGraphBundleRunsPromptPrefillAndDynamicKvDecode asserts host-session KV tensor identity. The external TensorRT device-session full-generation test asserts EOS, first three token IDs, and exact full table text.
kvBufferOptimization.measuredOutcome: Same official image and TensorRT device: generic strict-FP32 host-KV path 83.42 s; optimized device-resident TF32 path best observed 10.12 s (8.25x lower wall time than the old TensorRT route and 3.93x faster than the recorded ORT CPU run), with identical text. These are non-locked-clock observations, not a controlled multi-run benchmark.

tensorRtBuilderRegression.runtime: TensorRT 10.11.0.33, CUDA 12.9, cuDNN 9.22, RTX 3060 Laptop GPU 6GB, Windows 10, compute capability 8.6
tensorRtBuilderRegression.rootCause: The failing test resolved the plain ONNX decoder variant instead of the epsilon-patched graph used by the release path and gave attention_mask opt length 512 while the matching past_key/past_value opt length was 512. Since attention_mask length must be past + 1, TensorRT rejected a reshape from volume 512 to 513 and returned null from buildSerializedNetwork.
fix: Resolve *-epsilon.onnx before the plain ONNX graph, matching the release publisher and plan build script.
Set decoder attention_mask profile opt length to 513 when the past KV optimum is 512.
Retain TensorRT native logger messages in TensorRtBackendException.TechnicalDetails so future builder failures expose the native shape diagnostic.
Read ONNX opset metadata without materializing multi-gigabyte protobuf graphs for modern opsets.

fourBuilderPlanE2E.result: all four library-built TensorRT plans completed greedy generation to EOS and reproduced the exact official six-row table

chartQaHumanTensorRtEvidence.runtime: TensorRT 10.11.0, CUDA 12.9, cuDNN 9.22, RTX 3060 Laptop GPU 6GB; library-built strict-FP32 text plans, FP16 vision/embedding plans
chartQaHumanTensorRtEvidence.resultBoundary: All four runs reached EOS and exact expected generated-table strings; 8/8 labels were checked against values/counts derivable from the output tables. This is a 4-chart sample, not a benchmark-wide score. The 29m19s aggregate wall time was unexpectedly long versus the separate optimized official-sample observation. This run used Builder-created strict-FP32 text plans without a locked GPU clock; the timing cause has not been isolated and must not be used as a performance claim until a controlled rerun/profile.
